clue.text: The flower of detective fiction

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a pink or white wild flower of the pink family
second meaning: Albert ..., Margery Allingham's gentleman sleuth

explanation.surface: It reads like a tribute to the finest writer of detective stories.
explanation.walkthrough: Albert Campion is the detective hero of Margery Allingham's novels; the same word names a wild flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to a common hedgerow bloom and to a famous fictional sleuth of the Golden Age.

clue.text: The last thing one has to eat?

definitions.text: The last thing one has to eat?

parts.words: The last thing one has to eat?
parts.note: surface reading: the final item of food anyone must consume
setter's reading: the idiom for being finished or dying, having had one's portion of fried potato

explanation.surface: A diner faces the final morsel left on the plate.
explanation.walkthrough: To have had one's chips is British slang for being done for or dead, so the last thing anyone has is this fried food.
explanation.definitionFit: Fried potato strips are something eaten, and the idiom about having had them means reaching the end.

clue.text: Tea amid honey rendered by angel

indicators.note: amid means in the middle of, so one piece is set inside the other

parts.note: honey rendered into French is miel

explanation.surface: Someone serves tea sweetened with honey, prepared by a heavenly helper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rendered' here means translated: honey in French. The tea sits in the middle of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Michael is the archangel who leads the heavenly host against Satan in scripture and tradition.

clue.text: Name of the Fair Maid of Perth

indicators.note: of here means taken out of, so the name is drawn from within the phrase that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the join of the two words
surface padding completing the title of Scott's novel

explanation.surface: A quiz question asking for the name of the heroine of Scott's novel set in Perth.
explanation.walkthrough: Scott's Fair Maid of Perth is Catharine Glover, so the surface misleads; the name is spelt out inside the words themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Irma is a woman's first name, so it serves as an example of a name.

clue.text: Lines the Muse made Landor utter at exit on an adventure

indicators.note: the Muse composes, making verse out of raw material, so the words that follow are reworked into poetry

parts.words: Landor utter at exit on an adventure
parts.note: every letter of these words is used

explanation.surface: Inspired by the Muse, the dying poet speaks memorable last words.
explanation.walkthrough: Walter Savage Landor's 'Dying Speech of an Old Philosopher' runs: I strove with none, for none was worth my strife; nature I loved, and next to nature, art. The word adventure itself is part of the anagram, the rest acting as signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The quoted line comes from the short poem Landor wrote as his own deathbed farewell, his words on departing life.

clue.text: The flower (when with child) of the Exchequer

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the plant called love-in-a-mist
second meaning: the cookery writer ... Lawson, daughter of Chancellor Nigel Lawson

explanation.surface: It sounds like a fanciful title for the finest offspring of the Treasury.
explanation.walkthrough: Nigel Lawson was Chancellor of the Exchequer, Britain's finance minister, in the 1980s; his daughter is the television cook.
explanation.definitionFit: The blue garden plant shares its name with the famous food writer born to a former finance minister.

clue.text: See 4
Rulers turn green, detaining Vikings briefly

indicators.note: detaining means holding someone in custody, so one piece is held within another

parts.note: vert is green in heraldry and French
Northmen shortened by keeping only the initial of the first part

explanation.surface: Politicians go pale with envy while holding Norse raiders prisoner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn green' looks like an anagram hint or a description of sickness; it is two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The body that governs a country is the collective group of people ruling it.

clue.text: Lillian G. keeps on being fairly extended

indicators.note: keeps means holds onto, so the actress's name holds the little word inside it

parts.note: the silent film star Lillian Gish, here read as initial L and surname

explanation.surface: An actress named Lillian G. keeps going on at some length.
explanation.walkthrough: Lillian Gish was a star of silent cinema; the G. stands for her surname, and her first name gives only its initial.
explanation.definitionFit: The suffix -ish softens an adjective, so the word means somewhat long rather than very long.

clue.text: I have a breakdown, but I can deal with it

definitions.text: I have a breakdown, but I can deal with it

parts.note: surface reading: a person admitting to a nervous collapse
setter's reading: someone whose job is breaking things down into parts, and who treats patients in crisis

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to a collapse yet insists they can cope.
explanation.walkthrough: A breakdown is both a nervous collapse and a detailed analysis; this professional produces the second and treats the first.
explanation.definitionFit: A psychoanalyst helps people through mental crises, and any analyst examines things by breaking them into parts.

clue.text: It's fashionable to cajole (including police) with money for the 6

indicators.note: including means taking in as part, so the police go inside the word for cajole

parts.note: the Met is London's Metropolitan Police

explanation.surface: Smartly sweet-talking officers along with a bribe for those in power.
explanation.walkthrough: The 6 refers to the answer to 6 down, GOVERNMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: This levy on earnings is collected by the state and funds public spending, so it is cash for the rulers.

clue.text: Uncle to Victoria and Albert with whatever heart you like?

indicators.note: heart is the centre, so the word for whatever becomes the middle of the museum's initials

parts.note: V and A, the familiar name of the London museum
surface padding: whatever you like is a single phrase

explanation.surface: A question about some royal relative and a whimsical choice of filling.
explanation.walkthrough: Uncle Vanya is Chekhov's play; the V&A is the Victoria and Albert Museum in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Chekhov's title character is known to the world as Uncle, so the word stands for him by allusion.

clue.text: Visit of supporter

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a period spent somewhere as a guest
second meaning: a prop or brace, as a ship's rope or a corset rib

explanation.surface: A fan drops in to see their team.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun the word means a sojourn somewhere and also a rope or strut that holds something up.

clue.text: Loud and angry about little boy deprived of energy by society

parts.note: f, forte, is loud in music

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for angry is placed round the boy
deprived of means having something taken away, so the energy symbol is removed

explanation.surface: A noisy, furious society scolds a small boy who has run out of steam.
explanation.walkthrough: Ernie loses its final E, and what is left sits in the middle of the word for cross.
explanation.definitionFit: A brotherhood, especially an American student club, is a society of members bound by common interests.

clue.text: Canal dweller, not broad in the 23

definitions.text: Canal dweller, not broad in the 23

parts.words: Canal dweller, not broad in the 23
parts.note: surface reading: a slim creature living in the waterway
setter's reading: 23 is the beam, a vessel's width, so a craft slim across its middle

explanation.surface: It describes a slim creature living in a canal.
explanation.walkthrough: The 23 refers to BEAM, the width of a ship; British canal boats are built about seven feet wide to fit the locks.
explanation.definitionFit: These long slim vessels are lived on along British waterways, and their width is limited by lock size.

clue.text: One left with the destroyer makes for blue paper

definitions.note: a description of what the answer does, standing for the noun

explanation.surface: Someone abandoned with a warship produces a blue page.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Destroyer' suggests a warship, but it is the Hindu goddess Kali.
explanation.definitionFit: A base solution turns red litmus test paper blue, which is the classic school chemistry test.

clue.text: American city at speed alien to pretty little girl

explanation.surface: Something from New York, rushing past, seems strange to a young girl.
explanation.definitionFit: The word, popularised by Nabokov, means a sexually precocious young girl, so a young attractive girl.

clue.text: I keep a number of lawyers from Prohibition

indicators.note: keep means hold, so the self holds the number and lawyers inside it

parts.note: the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Someone claims to protect lawyers from the dry era of American history.
explanation.walkthrough: Capital-P Prohibition suggests the American alcohol ban; it is just a general ban.
explanation.definitionFit: An official ban on trade with a country is a prohibition imposed by a government.

clue.text: What Keats called Death to make us feel a difference

indicators.note: making a difference means altering things, so these letters change their order

explanation.surface: A poet's view of mortality is offered as something to change how we feel.
explanation.walkthrough: In 'Ode to a Nightingale' Keats writes that he has been half in love with easeful Death.
explanation.definitionFit: Keats's ode uses this adjective, meaning peaceful and soothing, for the dying he half longed for.

clue.text: Mr Wooster of Mansfield Park has rights in 23

indicators.note: has means holds or contains, so the width word holds the rights within it

parts.note: two abbreviations for right, rt and r

explanation.surface: A literary quiz linking P.G. Wodehouse's hero to Jane Austen's novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Bertie Wooster's full first name is Bertram, and Sir Thomas Bertram's family are at the centre of Austen's Mansfield Park.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is Bertie Wooster's formal Christian name and also the surname of the family who own Austen's estate.

clue.text: Nurse's kind offer?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: gentle and caring, as a good nurse is
second meaning: a formal bid, as for a contract

explanation.surface: A nurse makes a generous proposal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nurse's kind offer' reads as one phrase; it splits after 'kind', which means gentle, not type.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means gentle and caring, while the noun means a formal bid or proposal of a price.

clue.text: Urgent information during departure

indicators.note: during means in the course of, so the information falls within the departure

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Pressing news arrives just as someone is leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pressing that demands immediate action is urgent, a more formal word for the same idea.

clue.text: Jack, Chuck and Damon: a Gothic fantasy

parts.note: Jack Straw, rebel of 1381 and Labour foreign secretary
Chuck Berry, the rock and roll guitarist
Damon Hill, Formula One world champion

explanation.surface: Three famous men named in a row as if starring in a Gothic tale.
explanation.walkthrough: Each first name stands for a famous surname. Strawberry Hill is Horace Walpole's mock-Gothic villa at Twickenham, near London.
explanation.definitionFit: Walpole's house is the celebrated early fantasy of the Gothic Revival style in English architecture.

clue.text: See 20
Cooked meal with a Slav interrupting concentration

definitions.note: the answer is a concentrated ray

indicators.note: cooked food has been worked over and changed, so these letters are rearranged
interrupting means breaking in on, so the Slav breaks into the middle of the mixture

parts.note: a meal plus the letter a

explanation.surface: A dinner is prepared while an Eastern European guest breaks someone's focus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With a Slav' looks like one unit, but the a goes into the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a ray is light concentrated into a narrow intense stream, hence a concentration of energy.

clue.text: See 22
Give up favouring energy

explanation.surface: Someone abandons their preference for vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: To go without something or relinquish it is to abstain, the sense of giving it up.

clue.text: Being au fait with other areas' news

indicators.note: other means different, so the letters are turned into a different word

explanation.surface: Staying informed about what is happening elsewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Au fait is French borrowing for well informed, and the noun means knowledge or consciousness of something.

clue.text: Restricted cover covers minimal finance

indicators.note: covers means goes over and encloses, so the lid encloses the small coin

parts.note: a tiny coin, as in the widow's mite

explanation.surface: An insurance policy with limits pays out only a small sum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover' and 'finance' suggest insurance; the cover is a lid.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something held within bounds, as in a limited edition or restricted access.

clue.text: Disposition restricting time of siren

indicators.note: restricting means confining, so the word for disposition confines the time abbreviation

explanation.surface: Someone's mood limits how long a siren goes on sounding.
explanation.definitionFit: A siren in myth lures sailors to ruin, so she is one who entices or seduces.
